study_notes.title: Electric Cells: Storing Energy in Chemicals

cell_types.Primary_Cells: Cannot be recharged once chemicals are used up (e.g., Simple Dry Cells).
cell_types.Secondary_Cells_Accumulators: Can be recharged by passing current through them in reverse (e.g., Car batteries, mobile phone batteries).
cell_types.visual_reference: [IMAGE_010: Illustration of a Car Battery vs. a AA Dry Cell]

the_dry_cell_anatomy.visual_reference: [IMAGE_011: Labeled Cross-section of a Dry Cell]
the_dry_cell_anatomy.Zinc_Can: Negative (-) terminal; also acts as the container.
the_dry_cell_anatomy.Ammonium_Chloride: The electrolyte paste that allows electrons to move.
the_dry_cell_anatomy.Manganese_IV_Oxide: The Depolarizer. It stops hydrogen bubbles from blocking current.
the_dry_cell_anatomy.Carbon_Rod: A non-metallic conductor (Graphite) in the center.

simple_wet_cells_and_problems.Structure: Zinc and Copper plates in Dilute Sulphuric Acid.
simple_wet_cells_and_problems.Polarization: Hydrogen bubbles cover the copper plate, making the bulb dim. Fixed by adding a depolarizer.
simple_wet_cells_and_problems.Local_Action: Impurities in zinc cause it to waste away. Fixed by coating zinc with mercury (Amalgamation).
simple_wet_cells_and_problems.visual_reference: [IMAGE_012: Diagram of Simple Cell with bubbles on plates]
